name: InterContinental Paris Le Grand Hotel
positioning: Second Empire grand hotel, opened in 1862 under Napoleon III, directly opposite the Opera Garnier in central Paris
best_for: Travelers who want a central Paris base facing the Opera Garnier, a block from the grand department stores
History lovers drawn to a Napoleon III-era hotel with a domed ballroom and a glass-roofed winter garden

facts.text: The hotel was inaugurated under Napoleon III.
The hotel opened in 1862 with a gala event hosted by Empress Eugenie.
Rooms and suites are decorated in a Second Empire style with contemporary touches.
Classic Rooms are decorated in rich colours in the Napoleon III style, with street or courtyard views and marble bathrooms.
Some rooms have a private balcony with views over the Parisian rooftops.
All rooms feature Byredo amenities and complimentary tea and coffee.
Cafe de la Paix, led by Chef Laurent Andre, has been a symbol of Parisian life since 1862 and overlooks the Opera Garnier.
The original Dry Martini was created at the hotel in 1904 by head bartender Franck Newman.
The Club Lounge is open daily and serves breakfast, afternoon tea and an evening reception with canapes.
The department stores Galeries Lafayette and Printemps are a block away.
The Palais Royal Gardens and the Louvre are about a 15-minute walk away.
A portrait of Sarah Bernhardt still graces the reception area.

highlights.text: The hotel is located directly opposite the Opera Garnier.
The five Signature Suites, designed by Pierre-Yves Rochon, have panoramic views over the rooftops of the Opera Garnier or the Eiffel Tower.
The listed Opera ballroom, the Salon Opera, has a 14-meter-high dome with gilding, arcades, caryatids and candelabras.
La Verriere is an 800-square-meter winter garden beneath a glass and metal atrium, for coffee, light dining or an aperitif.
The Algotherm Dermo Ocean Spa has the atmosphere of a Parisian apartment, with four single treatment rooms and one double suite.

considerations.text: The hotel does not have a pool, and the fitness room is small.
WhataHotel notes a busy central location with high foot traffic.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's luxury positioning.
